reasons: Both answers cover all four rubric items with nearly identical, accurate content: the absorption blockers, the 24-hour hepcidin rise favouring alternate-day dosing, deferring to the doctor with workup and IV iron, and the post-exercise hepcidin timing. B adds useful extras: the daily hepcidin rhythm that makes evening doses worse, H. pylori and PPI use as causes of poor absorption, an explicit warning not to keep raising the oral dose, and concrete RED-S signs. A's advice to act only on black stools when abdominal pain is also present is slightly weaker safety guidance, though B's is similar.
